nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Agroforestry systems_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What shift in cocoa farming practices has been observed since the promotion of hybrid cocoa varieties?
nodes.answer: There has been a shift away from traditional shaded cocoa agroforestry systems towards full-sun monocrop cocoa plantations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Agroforestry systems_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is agroforestry and why has it become a topic of interest?
nodes.answer: Agroforestry is the practice of integrating trees with agricultural crops, and it has gained interest as a climate change mitigation measure due to its ability to retain trees and regulate micro-climates, as well as provide diversified income streams.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Agroforestry systems_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How can agroforestry systems compare to full-sun systems in terms of total system output?
nodes.answer: With proper management, agroforestry systems can achieve up to 10 times the total system output, including non-cocoa harvests, compared to full-sun cocoa plantations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Sustainable agricultural practices|Agroforestry systems_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What regions in West Africa were involved in the studies distinguishing agroforestry cocoa systems from full-sun counterparts?
nodes.answer: The studies were conducted in Ghana and Cameroon.
